Usage: relate [OPTIONS] [--database PATH] [QUERY]
       relate <COMMAND> [ARGS]

Commands:
  query          Run a statement session (oneshot, stdin, or shell)
  clone          Copy a database into a new store and exit
  info           Print store metadata for a database without opening it
  pull           Copy a Neo4j/Aura subgraph into a database
  push           Copy a database subgraph into Neo4j/Aura
  skill          Install, inspect, or remove the embedded agent skill bundle
  upgrade        Update the relate binary (alias: update)
  telemetry      Manage anonymous usage metrics (on, off, status)
  lab            Import a directory tree or a git history into a graph (experimental)
  serve          Host the HTTP Query API and MCP surfaces on a database
  agent-context  Print the compact agent briefing (commands, flags, exit codes)

Options:
  -h, --help    Show this help and exit
  --version     Show version and license and exit (with --json: one JSON object)
  -d, --database PATH  Database directory, .rl bundle, or :memory: (default :memory:)
  --json        Output as JSON (indented on a terminal, compact when piped)
  --csv         Output as CSV
  --markdown    Output as Markdown
  --jsonl       Output as JSON Lines
  --toon        Output as TOON (one header line, one line per row)
  --noheader    Disable column headers
  --mode MODE   Set output mode (table, csv, json, jsonl, envelope, markdown, cypher, toon, speedscope)
                default: table on a terminal, jsonl when stdout is piped or redirected
                (toon instead of jsonl when agent mode is on)
  --format MODE Alias of --mode
  --pretty      Indent JSON output even when stdout is not a terminal
  --param N=V   Bind a Cypher parameter (repeatable; V parsed as JSON scalar, bare words are strings)
  --fetch-params N=SRC  Fetch a URL or read a file (http, https, file path), parse it as JSON, and bind it as the parameter N (repeatable)
  --snapshot-format F  Snapshot codec (parquet|json); empty directory only
  --wal-dir DIR        WAL directory (default <DATABASE>/wal)
  --checkpoint-interval-secs N  Timed checkpoint period; 0 disables
  --durability-mode MODE  WAL durability (full|everysecond|snapshot; default full)
  --logical-graph-size-limit SIZE  Live graph + index cap (bytes or mb/mib/gb/gib)
  --expression-memory-limit SIZE  Per-value expression build cap (bytes, mb/mib/gb/gib, or none)
                       Default: 256 MiB. Guards against one statement
                       building a pathological single value; raise it, or
                       pass none for known bulk pipelines
  --concurrent-logical-workspace-limit SIZE  Shared logical-workspace pool (bytes or mb/mib/gb/gib)
                       A positive value turns admission on. Omit, or an
                       unset RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT,
                       leaves it off. 0 is rejected
  --max-traversal-depth N  Largest explicit traversal hop bound (1-2000; default 500)
                       A query whose explicit hop bound exceeds this fails at
                       admission with TraversalDepthExceeded. This is a safety
                       limit, not a database limit: raising it risks a stack
                       overflow on small-stack platforms.
                       RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH sets the default
  --safe               Refuse agent-typical dangerous statement shapes; --no-safe
                       negates it. Refuses a new named node without a label, and
                       a MATCH read without LIMIT or a reducing aggregate
                       (collect() does not count). A policy, not a database
                       limit. RELATE_SAFE_MODE=1/0 sets the default; off
                       unless asked.
  --agent-mode         Force agent ergonomics on (the row cap's default and the
                       toon piped default); pairs with --max-rows.
                       --no-agent-mode turns them off (the -mode suffix stays
                       clear of the skill-install harness selector).
                       Precedence: the flag, then RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1/0,
                       then harness detection (piped runs only). The explicit
                       acts print a one-line announcement; detection stays silent
  --max-rows N         Print at most N rows per statement; 0 = unlimited.
                       Default: 100 under a detected agent harness with stdout
                       not a terminal, unlimited otherwise (RELATE_MAX_ROWS)
  --width N            Wrap the human table to N display columns; the widest
                       columns shrink and their cells wrap over lines.
                       Default: the terminal width, else an exported COLUMNS
                       (both floored at 20), else the natural width
  --timeout DURATION   Cancel a statement that runs longer (500ms, 10s, 2m;
                       bare number = seconds; 0 disables). Exit code 7
  --read-only[=FRESH]  Open an existing database without writing or checkpointing.
                       FRESH is snapshot (default: a frozen snapshot at open) or
                       live (tail the WAL and follow the writer's commits;
                       refused for .rl and :memory:). Attach the value
                       (--read-only=live); once per run.
                       A native directory can be open beside a writer. A .rl file
                       opens only while no writer holds it. :memory: rejects writes
                       and creates nothing
  --load-csv-dir PATH  Allow local LOAD CSV under this directory (default denied; overrides RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR)
  --namespace NAME     Session namespace (neo4j|system|system_ontologies; default neo4j)
  -c, --command Q      One-shot statement or `;`-separated list (same as positional QUERY)
  --            Treat all following arguments as positional
On a TTY, the interactive shell supports readline-style editing (arrow keys, Home/End).

--database is a directory (WAL + snapshot), a .rl bundle, or :memory: (the default).
With no QUERY, the interactive shell opens on a terminal; on piped
or redirected stdin this help is printed. `query` with no STATEMENT reads a script
from stdin, or opens the same shell on a terminal.

Examples:
  # Run a query and print JSON
  relate --database ./mydata --json -c "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes"
  # Explore without being able to change anything
  relate --database ./mydata --read-only --mode envelope -c "MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n.name LIMIT 5"

Run 'relate <COMMAND> --help' for details on a command.
